messages:
maya: customer reported repeated case where SSE stream returns a small chunk then goes silent for ~2-3 minutes, client reconnects and resumes, causing duplicate token billing. they sent traces and a curl repro.

sam: thanks — can you paste the minimal repro here? is this only via ALB/ELB or also direct to dedicated instance?

maya: pasted curl below from customer (they said direct dedicated and via ALB both show issues intermittently):

maya: ```bash
curl -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \n  -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \n  'https://dedicated.example.redwood/api/v1/streams?model=rw-large'
```

maya: their client logs show first data chunk at 00:00:01, final partial chunk at 00:00:03, then silence until 00:02:05 when TCP FIN and reconnect. server logs show no error and tokens billed for both sessions.

ara: do we have any proxy idle timeouts in the path? ALB defaults ~350s, nginx often 60s, some corp proxies 90s. 2 minutes is suspiciously close to some intermediate timeout + delayed FIN.

sam: I pulled the trace — TCP keepalive was disabled on the client. On our side, the runtime didn't emit an SSE comment/ping after the final chunk because we thought the stream was complete. The connection stayed open server-side, no write activity, and a middlebox apparently reset it after ~125s.

customer-rep: customer insists client uses websocket fallback that reconnects aggressively after 90s of silence. they see 2 sessions with overlapping token ranges. billing flagged as duplicate.

maya: repro notes: customer suggests adding a server comment ping every 15s prevents the proxy from closing and avoids duplicate sessions. But that changes billing heuristics since we now keep sockets longer for idle users.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2024-0924. Assigned to sam and ara. :spiral_note_pad:

ara: suggested mitigations: add optional SSE comment ping header for `X-Redwood-keepalive: 15s` (app-level keepalive), document TCP keepalive recommendations for SDKs, and add server-side session lease: if no client ACK or progress for >90s mark stream stale and emit a final EOE event so client can resume cleanly using last-event-id/resume token.

sam: quick patch we can do: 1) enable comment pings by default for Dedicated behind common proxies (15s), 2) expose a config to opt-out for low-latency short requests, 3) add duplicate-detection token on resume (resume_id + last_seq) to avoid double billing if client resumes overlapping chunk ranges.

maya: also add a note to support runbook: if customer sees partial output + long silence -> ask for tcpdump, middlebox path, and whether client set TCP keepalive; suggest temporary client-side keepalive loop or shorter reconnect backoff until we roll patch.

customer-rep: customer agreed to try a client-side comment ping patch tonight and will report. they asked for ETA on server-side safe resume change.

sam: ETA for config + comment-ping rollout to staging 48h, safe-resume dedupe requires a small platform change (resume metadata) — estimate 5 working days.

ara: logging followups: add `last_write_ts` per stream to metrics + alert if stream silent >60s while connection open (support tier) so we can proactively notify customers.

maya: thanks team. I'll update the customer and attach this thread to INC-2024-0924. keeping this thread open for repro results. :thumbsup:
